note: Machine-readable expected outcome per fixture. Not one of the twelve files Contracts section 9 locks -- scaffolding, so that the AI lane's tests and the backend lane's ingest tests assert the same table instead of two drifting copies of it. Read this, do not retype it.

ingest_path_disagreement.problem: Contracts 6.1 says POST /api/v1/events/vehicle-sighting and returns 200 for a new event. The backend manual section 5.1 says POST /api/v1/ingest/events and returns 201 for a new event. Both documents are in docs/. They cannot both be right and nobody noticed until the fixtures needed an expected status code.
ingest_path_disagreement.resolution_pending: Needs one decision from the team, recorded in Contracts 6.1. Until then the AI worker defaults to /api/v1/ingest/events, because that is what the person implementing the endpoint is reading, and ai/emit/http_sink.py treats 200-with-status-accepted and 201 as the same outcome so either backend is accepted without a code change.

ai_event_high_confidence.json.why: Exact watchlist match on GJ01AB1234, four agreeing observations. The only fixture that may raise a confirmed alert.

ai_event_low_confidence.json.why: One observation at 0.51. Contracts 3.4: a weak observation must not reach ALERTED.

ai_event_unreadable.json.why: plate is null: no plate was located. Contracts 3.2 -- a valid, expected, correct event. Rejecting it would make the pipeline hide vehicles it could not identify, which is the opposite of what a police system needs.

ai_event_duplicate.json.why: Byte-identical to ai_event_high_confidence.json, which is what a retry after an ambiguous timeout looks like. Must not create a second sighting and must not raise a second alert. Order matters: POST high_confidence first.

ai_event_bad_timestamp.json.why: observed_at is naive. Ambiguous by up to a day, and the ambiguity surfaces as a journey with its events out of order. Never coerce.

ai_event_unknown_camera.json.why: locally_valid is true on purpose. cam99 is a well-formed Sentinel ID, so the AI lane's validator passes it -- existence is the catalogue's business, not the envelope's. This is the one fixture that separates shape validation from the database lookup, and a backend that rejects it with VALIDATION_FAILED instead of UNKNOWN_CAMERA has collapsed the two.

camera_reconnect.json.why: Contracts 1.2. Same camera, same track_id 42, different stream_session_id. One row means uq_trackkey is keyed on (camera_id, track_id) and every journey built from that data merges two vehicles.

scene_discontinuity.json.why: source_pts_ms goes 892300 then 1200. A backwards timeline means the frames are not from one continuous recording, so the session must rotate.

journey_four_cameras.json.why: The negative control for the feasibility check. Three segments at 16 to 22 km/h, all under the 150 km/h ceiling. A check that flags these is useless.

journey_implausible.json.why: 8.333 km in 2 seconds is 15000 km/h. The segment is flagged and BOTH sightings stay in the response. Contracts 4.5 forbids deleting the implausible one.

watchlist_match.json.why: Three seeded entries, one active exact match. The deactivated entry and the one-character-off plate are both in the file so a test can prove the matcher is selective rather than permissive.

search_response.json.why: Not POSTable. The canonical GET /api/v1/search/vehicles body, exact and fuzzy variants, for the frontend's generated types and its mocks.
